questions.problem: Find the domain of the function  $f(x,y)=\operatorname{arcsin}⁡({x}^{2}+y).$
questions.worked_solution:
The function is well-defined at all points $(x,y)$ for which the following condition is satisfied:

- The argument of the arcsine has values between $-1$ and $1.$

As a result, the points in the domain must satisfy the following inequality:

$$
-1\le {x}^{2}+y\le 1
$$

Therefore, the domain is

$$
\{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,-1\le {x}^{2}+y\le 1\}.
$$

We start by creating a matrix whose columns are made up of our vectors, and then we reduce the matrix to row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & -1 \\ 0 & 5 & 5 \\ -1 & 3 & -2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & -1 \\ 0 & 5 & 5 \\ 0 & \frac{3}{2} & -\frac{5}{2}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-\frac{3}{10}){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & -1 \\ 0 & 5 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & -4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The pivot columns correspond to basis vectors, while the non-pivot columns correspond to linearly dependent vectors that can be removed. Here, the reduced matrix has $3$ pivot columns (or alternatively, it has exactly $3$ non-zero rows). 

Therefore, the dimension of the span is $3.$

questions.problem: The discrete random variable $X\in Z$ can be approximated by the continuous random variable $Y.$ By applying an appropriate continuity correction, $P(X>-15)$ can be approximated as
questions.worked_solution:
To apply the appropriate continuity correction, we first rewrite the strict inequality as follows:

$$
P(X>-15)=P(X\ge -14)
$$

Then, we extend the endpoint of the interval $X\ge -14$ by $0.5:$

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\ge -14) & ≈P(Y\ge -14-0.5) \\  & =P(Y\ge -14.5)\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the orthogonal set $U$ below. By adding a new vector $x=[{x}_{1},\,{x}_{2},\,{x}_{3}]^{T},$ extend the set so that it forms an orthogonal basis of ${R}^{3}.$ What is the value of $\frac{{x}_{1}}{{x}_{2}}?$

$$
U=\{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -3 \\ 6\end{aligned}]\}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $U$ as ${u}_{1},\,{u}_{2}.$ To extend the given set to an orthogonal basis of ${R}^{3}$, we need to find a third vector $x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]$ such that

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{u}_{1}\cdot x=0 \\ {u}_{2}\cdot x=0\end{aligned}\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=0 \\ -3{x}_{2}+6{x}_{3}=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we consider the augmented matrix $M$ of the system above, which is already in row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -3 & 6 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns ($1$st and $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we get ${x}_{2}=2{x}_{3}.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2(2{x}_{3})+{x}_{3}=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=-5{x}_{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-5{x}_{3} \\ 2{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Setting ${x}_{3}=1,$ we obtain the vector 

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, an orthogonal basis of ${R}^{3}$ is

$$
\{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -3 \\ 6\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\}.
$$

Finally, $\frac{{x}_{1}}{{x}_{2}}=\frac{-5}{2}=-\frac{5}{2}.$

questions.problem:
Suppose ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{9}$ is an I.I.D random sample with ${X}_{i}∼B(7,\theta )$ and unknown probability of success $\theta .$ For a particular sample ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{9},$ you're given that 

$$
{\sum }_{i=1}^{9}{x}_{i}=13.
$$

Find the likelihood function of the sample up to a constant $C.$

*Hint: The probability mass function for a binomial random variable is given by*

$$
f(x)=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{x}){\theta }^{x}(1-\theta )^{n-x},\,x=0,1,2,…,n.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that if ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ are independent and identically distributed discrete random variables with probability mass function $f(x;\theta ),$ where $\theta $ is an unknown parameter, then the likelihood function of a random sample ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ is

$$
L(\theta )=P({X}_{1}={x}_{1},{X}_{2}={x}_{2},…,{X}_{n}={x}_{n})={\prod }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i};\,\theta ).
$$

In our case, we are given a sample of $n=9$ independent binomial random variables with unknown probability of success $\theta $ and $N=7$ trials, for which the probability mass function is

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x;\theta )=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{7}{x}){\theta }^{x}(1-\theta )^{7-x}, & \,x=0,1,2,…,7.\end{aligned}
$$

We can calculate the likelihood function as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}L(\theta ) & ={\prod }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i};\theta ) \\  & ={\prod }_{i=1}^{n}(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{7}{{x}_{i}}){\theta }^{{x}_{i}}(1-\theta )^{7-{x}_{i}} \\  & =((\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{7}{{x}_{1}}){\theta }^{{x}_{1}}(1-\theta )^{7-{x}_{1}})\cdot ((\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{7}{{x}_{2}}){\theta }^{{x}_{2}}(1-\theta )^{7-{x}_{2}})⋯((\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{7}{{x}_{n}}){\theta }^{{x}_{n}}(1-\theta )^{7-{x}_{n}}) \\  & =C\,{\theta }^{\,\sum {x}_{i}}(1-\theta )^{\,\sum (7-{x}_{i})} \\  & =C\,{\theta }^{\,\sum {x}_{i}}(1-\theta )^{\,7n-\sum {x}_{i}} \\  & =C\,{\theta }^{S}(1-\theta )^{7n-S}\end{aligned}
$$

where $C={\prod }_{i=1}^{n}(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{7}{{x}_{i}})$ is a constant and $S={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}.$

We are told that $S={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}=13$ and $n=9.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}L(\theta ) & =C\,{\theta }^{13}(1-\theta )^{7(9)-13} \\  & =C\,{\theta }^{13}(1-\theta )^{50}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: In winter, the maximum daily temperature of a certain mountain location (rounded to the nearest degree) varies between $-{15}^{∘}C$ and ${2}^{∘}C,$ inclusive. Assuming that for a given winter day, each maximum temperature value between $-{15}^{∘}C$ and ${2}^{∘}C$ has an equal probability of occurring, what is the probability that the maximum daily temperature will reach at least ${0}^{∘}C$ on a randomly selected day?
questions.worked_solution:
Let $X$ represent the maximum daily temperature (rounded to the nearest degree Celsius). From the problem statement, we know that $X∼U\{-15,-14,…,2\},$ and we wish to compute $P(X\ge 0).$

In general, if $X$ follows a discrete uniform distribution over a set $S,$ then $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{|S|}, & x\in S \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Here, we have $X∼U\{-15,-14,…,2\},$ and the set $S=\{-15,-14,…,2\}$ has $|S|=2-(-15)+1=18$ items. So, we have

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{18}, & x=-15,-14,…,2 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

In $S,$ the items that satisfy $X\ge 0$ are $0,1,2.$ There are $3$ of these elements. Therefore,

$$
P(X\ge 0)=3\cdot \frac{1}{18}=\frac{1}{6}.
$$

questions.problem:
$\,$ Either go to the movies, or you can watch a film at home.

Which conditional statement is logically equivalent to the disjunctive statement above?
questions.worked_solution:
Let's denote by $A$ and $B$ the following statements:

- $A:$ Go to the movies.

- $B:$ You can watch a film at home.

Then, our initial statement can be written as $A∨B,$ which is logically equivalent to 

$$
¬A⇒B.
$$

The negation of $A$ can be written as

- $¬A:$ You don't go to the movies.

Therefore, the given statement is logically equivalent to the following:

$\,$ If you don't go to the movies, then you can watch a film at home.

**Note**: 

Using the word "Either" helps clarify that the sentence structure presents two alternatives and is particularly useful when employing the disjunctive form $(¬P∨Q)$ in conversational or formal English. So, the phrase effectively conveys that one of the two stated conditions will hold true.

Compute $P(X=2\,\,\text{and}\,\,Y\le 4)$ given that the random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ shown in the table above.
questions.worked_solution:
Using the values in the table, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=2\,\,\text{and}\,\,Y\le 4) & =P((X,Y)\in \{(2,2),(2,4)\}) \\  & =P((X,Y)=(2,2))+P((X,Y)=(2,4)) \\  & =f(2,2)+f(2,4) \\  & =0.05+0.15 \\  & =0.2.\end{aligned}
$$
